transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-06 15:00 UTC — Duration: 42 mins. Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Ethan Liu (Redwood SE); Nora Kim (Redwood CSM); Priya Desai (Harbor, Lead ML Eng); Carlos Mendez (Harbor, Platform Eng); Leah Thompson (Harbor, PM); Tom Bauer (Harbor, SRE).

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: SDK integration notes, function calling edge cases, structured output contract, and then metrics/acceptance. if we can keep to 40 minutes that would be great.

[00:22] Priya (Harbor): Thanks Maya. quick update from our side — we ran the SDK on staging last night, saw a handful of errors when invoking the external tool hooks. mostly 502-ish, sometimes JSON parse errors on returned payload. not sure if it's the SDK middleware or the function call plumbing.

[00:41] Ethan (Redwood SE): ok thanks Priya, can you paste one of the payloads in the sheet? sometimes the SDK will wrap the response with an additional metadata envelope and if the downstream validator expects raw array it fails. also curious if you enabled streaming; streaming + tool calling can produce partial chunks that look like invalid json if you try to parse early.

[01:05] Carlos (Harbor): we are not streaming — just single-shot calls. the error log shows intermittent 502 from the redwood gateway, sequences like 'kv cache miss' then a spike in latency. i'm not sure if that's a mis-typed K V cache in the logs or an actual cache eviction.

[01:28] Ethan: yeah sometimes the auto-transcribed logs call it K V cache. but behind the scenes it's our prefix/KV cache. eviction could be due to sequence length or memory pressure from another tenant in the shared sandbox. for the pilot we recommend isolated dedicated pool or pinning a model variant to avoid noisy neighbors.

[01:55] Tom (Harbor SRE): we're trying to stay on hosted for now until acceptance. dedicated is a later conversation. question: for POC acceptance we need consistent p95 under 250ms for short prompts (<64 tokens). is that realistic on hosted with batching?

[02:12] Maya: good question. with conservative batching and prefix caching, we can hit p95 ~180–220ms on the smaller model variants in most regions, but it depends on traffic burstiness. if you need strict SLOs, Dedicated or reserved capacity is safer. we can also suggest quantized model variants to lower latency. tradeoff: a small quality delta.

[02:40] Leah (Product): quality delta — can you quantify that? our product owner will not accept hallucination regressions.

[02:50] Ethan: rough numbers — top-line: quantization to int8-ish gives ~10–14% lower token quality on some specialist models for long-context summarization, but for short classification/slot-filling tasks it's negligible. we'll run a quick regression set against your acceptance prompts.

[03:07] Priya: we'll share a ~200-prompt acceptance set; includes edge cases for dates, currency formatting, and nested arrays. also need deterministic structured output: schema is strict JSON with fields: transaction_id, verdict, confidence, evidence[]. if function calling returns a wrapped object we saw an extra meta.header field which breaks our pipeline.

[03:34] Ethan: ok, so structured-output contract is strict. recommended pattern: use the SDK's function-calling shim and pass a JSON schema to the model call; Redwood's structured output post-processor will validate and return either the parsed object or a standardized error payload so you can treat failures deterministically. we'll include sample code.

[03:59] Priya: we tried the signature you suggested, but our test harness reported 'schema mismatch: trailing comma' which looked like a serializing bug in our client. could also be the SDK's naive serializer when nested arrays contain nulls.

[04:22] Maya: that's plausibly client side. two quick asks: 1) can Harbor share the exact failing payload and the SDK version — sometimes older SDK builds had a serializer edge-case fixed in v0.9.4; 2) Redwood will instrument additional logging in the sandbox to capture the raw wire bytes for those failed calls.

[04:42] Carlos: noted, we'll paste the payloads in the sheet. another item — security: we need to confirm KMS key flow and that logs don't contain PII. do you have a SOC2 package?

[04:58] Nora (Redwood CSM): yes we circulated our SOC2 Type II summary earlier; i'll re-share the link. on KMS: for Private/enterprise deployments we support customer-managed keys and HSM-backed rotation. for hosted you can either use Redwood-managed keys or bring-your-own via a KMS integration (we have docs).

[05:20] Tom: for this pilot we need a sample policy so our security team can sign off. will send a stub of required key policy.

[05:33] Ethan: great. back to function/tool calling — we observed two failure classes in your logs: (A) model returns invalid json (truncated streaming chunk), (B) external tool errors passed through without standardized error wrapper. we recommend implementing a small retry wrapper with idempotency keys for your tool endpoints; Redwood can also optionally apply the canonical error envelope for you if you enable the 'strict function mode' in the SDK.

[06:05] Priya: would enabling strict function mode change cost or latency?

[06:12] Ethan: slight overhead — maybe +5–8ms per call due to validation step and additional serialization, negligible compared to network. no cost delta beyond tokens.

[06:25] Leah: acceptance metrics — to be explicit: 1) structured-output parse success >= 98% on the acceptance set, 2) p95 latency < 250ms for short prompts, 3) error rate < 0.2% for function calls under baseline load. can Redwood confirm those are measurable from the console?

[06:44] Maya: yes our Console will report token-level latencies and per-route error rates; we can also surface structured-output parse metrics once we run the validation job. we'll add those as custom dashboards for Harbor so you don't need to stitch logs.

[07:00] Carlos: one more infra question — our infra team needs sample CIDRs and egress IPs for whitelisting. is that static for the sandbox?

[07:12] Nora: sandbox is shared and IPs are not static; for restricted environments we recommend a Dedicated or Private deployment. however we can provide an ephemeral list for the benchmark window and the dedicated pool option has stable egress.

[07:28] Tom: ok, for now we'll request ephemeral whitelist for the test window.

[07:35] Ethan: on the test plan: Redwood will run a 5k prompt batch including your acceptance set and an adversarial subset (nulls, broken json, nested arrays). we'll capture the parse success, false positive/neg rates, and token costs. we'll publish a shared spreadsheet with per-prompt outputs and the validation status.

[07:58] Priya: perfect. couple of edge-cases: nested arrays inside evidence[] sometimes get normalized to strings by our validator if there's an extra comma. also timezone normalization for dates — sometimes model yields US format vs ISO. we'd like canonicalizers in the pipeline or enforced via schema patterns.

[08:24] Ethan: we can include canonicalization hooks in the SDK example — a small post-processor that runs regex/dateutil and normalizes before final validation. Redwood's structured-output toolkit supports pluggable post-processors. we'll demo that in the playbook.

[08:42] Leah: on rollout strategy — after acceptance, we'd like a canary rollout to 5% of traffic with automatic fallback to a safe model variant. is that supported?

[08:55] Maya: yes, Redwood supports canary/A B style rollouts with automatic fallback policies based on error budget and quality regressions. we can set the rollout policy in the Console and tie it to model metrics.

[09:10] Carlos: who owns the quality thresholds during the pilot? product or ML team?

[09:18] Leah: Product will own final sign-off but ML will provide the validation scripts.

[09:26] Maya: ok we'll include a suggested acceptance doc and leave placeholders for your thresholds.

[09:34] Tom: regarding cost — can you give rough token cost estimate for the 5k run and for steady-state 100K monthly requests?

[09:42] Maya: yes we'll include a cost model. quick back-of-envelope: the 5k run should be low hundreds of dollars depending on model variant; steady state depends heavily on average tokens per request and batching — we'll prepare a breakdown per-route.

[10:00] Priya: one blocker we saw: SDK version mismatch across dev teams; frontend is on v0.9.1 and backend on v0.9.4. older builds had different function-calling serializers. can Redwood give a recommended pinned version for the pilot?

[10:17] Ethan: recommend v0.9.6 (contains streaming fixes and strict function mode). we'll attach the changelog and a migration guide.

[10:30] Nora: action summary — Redwood will run the structured-output batch, instrument sandbox logs, share pinned SDK version and playbook. Harbor will share acceptance prompts, failing payloads, and whitelist requirements.

[10:45] Leah: timeline — assume Redwood runs tests by 2026-05-09 and we reconvene next Tuesday. does that work?

[10:52] Maya: yes we'll aim to have results and the shared spreadsheet by then. last quick question from me — any regulatory constraints on storing even ephemeral logs in shared sandboxes?

[11:03] Tom: Harbor can't store PCI data in shared sandboxes; we already scrub sensitive fields but need proof of scrubbing. will add to action items.

[11:18] Maya: understood we will add logging scrubbing notes and show where in the pipeline PII is redacted.

[11:30] Maya: ok thanks everyone, recap: Redwood runs benchmark and structured-output validation, shares results and playbook, Harbor provides prompts and payloads, security items to be circulated. reconvene next Tue 2026-05-12 15:00 UTC (tentative).

[11:48] Leah: thanks all.

[11:51] (meeting ends)

Notes / attachments referenced: shared spreadsheet link (redwood: //playbooks/harbor-structured-output) ; SOC2 summary link (redwood-sec/docs/soc2-summary.pdf) ; sandbox benchmark link (https://redwood.app/pilot/harbor/benchmarks).
